The Experience

Salesforce’s pre-sales Technical Architects (TAs) are the solutions team members who know what’s possible and how to make it happen, no matter how complex the challenge appears to be. Their domain and product knowledge allows them to serve as subject matter experts on the account team, not only in terms of product and domain knowledge, but also in how to craft the right solutions to satisfy both business and IT buyers. They are not afraid to dig into the inner workings of our platform to answer a challenging question or address an objection, and are equally comfortable speaking to a room of software developers as they are to the CIO & CTO.

As hands-on technical leaders, TAs take an active role in leading and executing Proof of Concepts (POCs) during customer engagements, working alongside the pre-sales team to demonstrate real-world value and validate solution approaches. They translate customer requirements into working prototypes, leveraging their deep technical expertise to de-risk implementations and accelerate time-to-value.

They are willing to be honest about potential challenges and always keep the long-term success of the customer in mind. People who enjoy both working with technology in a deep way and relating to people will excel in this role. Curiosity, communication, and capacity for learning are key pillars for successful TAs.

The SMB EMEA Technical Architect works with Salesforce’s Small & Medium Business (SMB) customers across all industries. As pre-sales engineers and architects, we partner with our customers to drive digital transformation within their companies, and support the sales team in winning new business. We work in a fast-paced, team-driven collaborative environment where everyone brings something unique to the table to get the job done.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Work with EMEA SMB customers in close collaboration with our sales and solution engineering teams, to solve a wide variety of technical challenges using the whole portfolio of Salesforce solutions.
  • Develop relationships, and act as a trusted advisor to CIO/CTO/CISO and their teams, as they integrate Salesforce into their technology strategy, guiding them towards long-term success.
  • Understand customer’s needs and establish Salesforce’s product as the best solution that addresses the technical and business requirements.
  • Present Salesforce technology infrastructure, including demonstrating deep familiarity with platform capabilities, hosting infrastructure, security and integration capabilities.
  • Conduct architecture and technical workshops, providing actionable technical recommendations that are aligned with the client’s business objectives.
  • Handle customer technical due diligence and risk management processes.
  • Partner with pre-sales teams to lead technical POCs, translating customer requirements into working demonstrations that validate solution feasibility and drive deal progression
  • Translate business requirements into solution architectures and roadmaps that best leverage the Salesforce platform and products with a successful implementation and adoption in mind
  • Participate in all appropriate product, sales, and procedural training and certification to acquire and maintain the knowledge necessary to be effective in the position.
  • Lead our SMB Technical Architect Community to enable less technical solutions colleagues and act as a multiplier.
  • Work closely with a variety of stakeholders e.g. alliances, sales programs, product & product marketing, etc. to develop and execute internal and external programs and initiatives.
  • Attain quarterly and annual objectives assigned by management.
  • Mentor, teach and guide more junior and less technical team members within the ESMB Solution Engineering organisation but also the Account Executive teams.



You're Our Person If...

  • Minimum 5 years working experience in a system architect, solution engineering role or a technical architect role or over 4 years experience in a SME/SMB or tech start up operations, consulting, implementation management, pre sales or solution engineering role

  • Strategic thinker, thought leadership and comfort communicating with executive audiences.
  • Excellent time management skills and the ability to support multiple, concurrent projects.
  • Lifelong learner, inquisitive, practical, and passionate about technology and sharing knowledge.

Even Better If...

The Experience

Developer Workspaces runs the computers Slack engineers write code on - and more and more, the ones AI agents write code on. Every week, hundreds of engineers build and test Slack in the remote development environments we run on AWS and Kubernetes. Now we're building the next layer: fast, isolated sandboxes where coding agents can run a dev toolchain, open pull requests, and shut down when they're done.


If most of Slack's code is going to be written by agents, it'll be written on infrastructure this team owns.


We're a small team with a lot of surface area. We're strong on backend engineering, and we need more depth in infrastructure and operations. That's this role. You'll own production systems early, carry the pager, and help decide how agents run safely at Slack.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Scale our AI sandbox fleet into something the whole company depends on - capacity planning, safe rollouts, image builds, and the alerts that tell us when it's breaking.
  • Harden the isolation between agents, sandboxes and the rest of Slack: network separation, egress controls, secrets handling, and patching.
  • Run and improve the remote dev environments our engineers use every day, from Terraform and machine images to the automation that pauses idle environments so they don't burn money.
  • Build observability we can make decisions with - SLOs, dashboards, and logs that land where we can find them.
  • Join our weekly on-call rotation once you've ramped up. Most pages are low urgency. When something does break, we fix it and then automate the fix.
  • Use AI agents heavily in your own work. You're building the platform they run on, so you should know what they need.

You're Our Person If...

  • You have 3+ years of experience building and operating production systems.
  • You come from infrastructure, SRE, DevOps or platform engineering, and you've been on call for something that mattered.
  • You know AWS well - EC2, networking, IAM - and you manage infrastructure as code with Terraform or something like it.
  • You write solid code in Go or Python. Everything we do ships as code, and your infrastructure instincts shape how you write it.
  • You use AI coding tools every day and have opinions about where they fall short.
  • You take ownership. When something breaks, you don't wait for someone to assign it to you.

Even Better If...

  • You've worked with Firecracker, KVM, or other virtualization.
  • You've run Kubernetes in production.
  • You have a security background: VM or container isolation, vulnerability management, threat modeling.
  • You're comfortable in Linux internals and networking.

To power AI and digital transformation initiatives, organizations must bring all of their data, systems, and processes together. In this role, you will drive adoption of MuleSoft’s products for customers on the Signature Success Plan, including renewals and growth across teams. You will work closely with Territory Sales, Renewals, Success Plan Sellers, Support, and Product teams. An ideal candidate has a strong background in Customer Success strategies, trends, and outcomes at the enterprise level, and can research, synthesize, and turn market intelligence and customer feedback into insights and action. We’re looking for customer focus, teamwork, resourcefulness, flexibility, and a get-it-done attitude.

  • Manage a team of 6-12 CSMs, fostering growth and excellence.
  • Resolve customer-blocking issues as a senior representative of Salesforce.
  • Implement strategies for Signature Success Plan renewals across teams.
  • Partner with peers and selling teams on capacity planning for Signature obligations.
  • Align customer allocations with Signature coverage, manage team-based allocations, and synchronize additional cloud resources as needed.
  • Oversee critical customer issues, working across Support, Critical Incident Center, and Engineering until resolution.
  • Work effectively in cross-functional teams (e.g., Sales, Support, Delivery), leveraging resources and building strong relationships internally and externally.
  • Manage escalations (support, relationship, and commercial) by setting a plan for the team, providing hands-on guidance and coaching, and stepping in when needed.

  • Demonstrated success driving incremental Annual Contract Value (iACV) through expansion sales and managing Net Revenue Retention (NRR) strategies and tactics.

You'll partner with Pricing Strategy, Product Management, Engineering, Finance, and Sales Operations, and your business requirements will influence the roadmap for our provisioning systems. This is a hybrid role with three days in office each week.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Own licensing and entitlement design for launches. Define the entitlement model for each offer: which features are on, which limits apply, and how capacity is provisioned and enforced.
  • Recommend license and entitlement structures to Product and Pricing teams, tying each option back to the business outcome you want.
  • Validate license and entitlement compatibility, and make sure each one maps correctly to license containers and to SKU and product records in our CRM.
  • Keep traceability from SKU to license to entitlement to feature, so every sellable item provisions what the customer bought.
  • Partner with Engineering and Provisioning on how entitlements behave in the product, including hard vs. soft limits, overage handling, and trial-to-paid conversion.
  • Build licensing governance into the NPI process for all new launches and repackaging efforts, moving strategy and technical validation earlier. Own license and entitlement sign-off for launches.
  • Train Product Operations project leads to run baseline project-level reviews, and rebalance review work between them and this role as NPI volume changes.
  • Create operating standards, including QA checklists, configuration menu options, and use cases. Develop enablement materials that support scalable, agentic question answering for product and pricing stakeholders.
  • Close current licensing gaps. Define an ownership model for cross-cloud licensing decisions between Product and Prod Ops (including legacy products), with a clear split of responsibility between Prod Ops and the Platform team. Build an M&A licensing playbook for bringing acquired-company user licensing into our model.
  • Assess financial and operational impact. Evaluate how usage-based pricing affects ACV, bookings, revenue recognition, forecasting, and sales compensation. Work with Finance, Deal Desk, and Sales Comp so new models fit approval workflows, discounting rules, and quota crediting.
  • Assess the experience each design creates for customers (buying, provisioning, usage visibility), sellers (quoting, configuration), and internal operators (order management, support, renewals).
  • Translate technical licensing capabilities and constraints into clear business terms, covering options, tradeoffs, and recommendations. Bring feasibility issues into packaging discussions early, before launch commitments are made.
  • Write and maintain launch documentation, standards, and playbooks. Build and maintain a central licensing resource with our provisioning team that shows which tools exist, who owns what, and how licensing choices affect commercial outcomes.



You're Our Person If...

  • You have 7+ years in product management, engineering, commercial operations, IT, or a similar role at a SaaS or enterprise software company, including 2+ years leading technical cross-functional programs.
  • You have experience constructing licensing or entitlements for B2B SaaS, or experience in the product and engineering development lifecycle for SaaS products.
  • You've taken new products or pricing models from packaging concept to launch as a product manager or engineer.
  • You can develop business and technical requirements that drive the product and engineering roadmap for license construction, data model enhancements, and stakeholder tooling.
  • You can read, write, and troubleshoot XML (structure, attributes, namespaces, schema validation) and catch errors in license and entitlement definitions before they reach production.
  • You use SOQL, SQL, and AI tools to query product, license, and entitlement data, find mapping gaps, and audit catalog consistency.
  • You can master the data model for licenses and entitlements and drive requirements to update it as commercial and product needs evolve.
  • You work with source control (e.g., Git) and structured engineering release processes for configuration changes.



Even Better If...

The Technical Analyst role is a part of the Quoting Rules team within the broader Product & Pricing Operations space. The work is fast-paced and broadly impactful across the company with various partner engagements. Responsibilities include helping craft scalable solutions and processes with engineers and architects, working with support teams who support customers and our internal systems, as well as taking business requirements to translate them into concrete technical requirements. To succeed, a candidate will need to be analytical, have excellent critical thinking skills, and be able to prioritize, deliver on multiple requests at once, identify inefficiencies in the process, and build scripts to help us continually improve.

This position is for the Hyderabad location only.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Design, implement, and manage the configuration of our internal CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) systems.
  • Own end-to-end governance of quoting rules, including impact analysis, UAT support, defect resolution, and continuous optimization of rule frameworks and production support
  • Proficiency in Q2C processes with the ability to proactively identify the upstream and downstream impact of business rules across related systems.
  • Strong understanding of New Product Introduction (NPI) processes, with proven experience collaborating effectively with cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Ability to translate complex technical requirements into clear, easy-to-understand language for functional and business stakeholders.
  • Design and develop Automation frameworks to reduce human efforts and increase team efficiency.
  • Support the operation and maintenance of existing and future CPQ infrastructure, including rule configuration, release management, environment management, data transformation, and migration.
  • Lead all aspects of troubleshooting and bug fixing for published rules configurations and case management.
  • Enable faster NPI and product launches by building reusable quoting rule patterns and automation frameworks that reduce manual intervention and errors.
  • Should have done at least two end-to-end implementation of a CPQ project.
  • Identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and areas for improvement in the product lifecycle.
  • Influence partners, facilitate and steer group conversations and be clear with expectations and timelines.
  • Should possess a keen eye for identifying and automating manual tasks using scripting solutions.
  • Flexible to support EMEA hours.
  • This is an Office based position out of the Hyderabad Office.

  • Excellent communication, written, and customer service skills.
  • Proven track record of leveraging generative AI tools (e.g., Claude) to drive measurable productivity gains, process improvements, and analytical outcomes within a team
  • Exceptional analytical, troubleshooting, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to manage workload with minimal supervision, prioritizing accuracy of deliverables.

As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), you will serve as a named resource and partner for Salesforce’s customer organizations. Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience


Salesforce is hiring a Portfolio Leader to directly manage and grow a team of technical AI specialists deploying Agentforce solutions inside complex customer environments. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can drive engineering excellence while operating at the executive level. This is not a traditional people manager, but a mission-critical multiplier on the agentic frontier. You will lead a blended delivery team made up of two specialist functions: Forward Deployed Engineers (Technical Builders - who design, build, and deploy AI Agents directly in customer environments) and Deployment Strategists (Strategic Builders - customer-facing advisors who shape AI strategy, define use cases, and drive adoption). Together, these teams work alongside customers to co-build and deliver agentic AI solutions on a single large enterprise account or across multiple engagements simultaneously. You'll set the engineering standards, unblock complex customer deployments, and scale the talent that's shipping production AI today.


Production leadership required. Builder mindset non-negotiable.


The Builder Leadership Experience

  • Delivery Team Coordination: You own the capacity planning, talent acquisition, and staffing that ensures your cross-functional squads have the horsepower to deploy Agentforce at enterprise scale.
  • AI-Augmented Leadership: Your team ships solutions using a best-in-class suite of AI tools (Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes). You will foster an inclusive, high-energy, and psychologically safe engineering culture where builders iterate fast and continuously level up.
  • Direct Product Influence: You stand at the center of the product feedback loop. Partner directly with the Product and Engineering organizations on pilot programs and beta rollouts, turning raw field insights from high-stakes deployments into features on the Agentforce core roadmap.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Scale Elite Talent: Recruit, mentor, and develop the next wave of Technical and Strategic Builders. Drive technical excellence, structure career growth, and foster an environment where shipping high-quality, production-ready systems is the norm.
  • Maintain Operational Velocity: Monitor key delivery metrics, coach your teams on optimization, and run hard on complex customer escalations. You ensure your teams move from sketch to deployable in weeks, not months.
  • Ultimate Technical Authority: Serve as the final technical escalation point for your portfolio. Maintain deep architectural judgment across the Salesforce platform, advanced LLM techniques, data pipelines, and agentic orchestration.
  • Guide Enterprise Implementations: Unblock complex data readiness, tool integration, and multi-agent orchestration challenges. Step in directly to help your teams assess customer technical readiness, remove deployment barriers, and codify standardized, repeatable delivery methodologies.
  • Drive Agentic Adoption: Build and anchor strong executive-level relationships within your customer portfolio, ensuring flawless Agentforce activation, rollout, and sustained production value.

The Experience

Production implementation experience required. Builder mindset non-negotiable.

Salesforce is hiring Forward Deployed Engineers focused on Data 360, Salesforce’s real-time data engine that unifies data from any source. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will be a hands-on Technical Builder who configures, builds, tests, and deploys Data 360 directly inside enterprise customer environments. You will turn approved solution designs and acceptance criteria into working implementations across ingestion, harmonization, identity, insights, activation, retrieval, security, and operational readiness.

Data 360 is also the data foundation for Agentforce - and grounding agents in accurate, real-time enterprise data is deep data engineering. You’ll go further into RAG, vector search, MCP, and agent-to-agent integration than most data roles ever touch, because the agents are only as good as the layer you build.

You’ll work within a delivery team that includes architects, deployment strategists, Agentforce FDEs, account teams, and customer technical teams. Engagements may span a focused proof, production rollout, and stabilization. The common thread is real customer data, disciplined testing, and a supportable handoff.

This is a hands-on data and software engineering role. You will build in real enterprise customer environments - writing SQL, Python, and Apex; building ingestion pipelines; debugging identity resolution; and shipping working implementations from sandbox through production. If you’re looking for a purely declarative configuration role or a pure advisory role, this isn’t it.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Build in customer environments. Configure and develop directly in customer sandboxes and production - using Data 360 configuration, SQL, Apex, Flow, Python, the REST Query API, the Interaction SDK, Salesforce DX, CLI, Git, Data Kits, and deployment tooling as required - following security, change-management, and release controls.
  • Engineer the data layer. Build ingestion, harmonization, and identity resolution across batch and streaming sources. Materialize views of data optimized for specific application, analytical, and agentic workloads, tuning latency and cost tradeoffs to meet use-case requirements. Work with customer data and AI teams to ensure implementations align with their existing strategies (e.g., data mesh, data fabric).
  • Prove it works. Create representative test data and validate expected outcomes across happy paths, edge cases, access boundaries, hierarchy behavior, failure conditions, and customer-scale volumes.
  • Ground the agents. Design, build, and maintain the AI data integration layer - RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), vector databases, search indexes, and knowledge bases - that grounds Agentforce solutions in accurate, real-time enterprise data.
  • Orchestrate agent communication. Design and implement the protocols - including Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent communication - that govern, monitor, and ensure efficient collaboration among specialized AI agents.
  • Connect the ecosystem. Implement robust, scalable, and secure data integration patterns that connect Agentforce to a wide range of enterprise applications and enable communication between AI agents.
  • Govern the data. Apply deep data management expertise to ensure the secure integration, transformation, and governance of structured and unstructured data across the Salesforce ecosystem (CRM, Data Cloud) and external systems.
  • Build for scale and security. Apply knowledge of message queues, event-driven architecture, and distributed systems to build resilient workflows and implement secure authentication and authorization protocols (OAuth, SAML) so that all agent actions are secure and comply with enterprise security policies.
  • Debug the hard problems. Troubleshoot ingestion failures, mapping defects, schema drift, identity anomalies, query behavior, activation latency, API errors, permissions, and consumption issues - methodically, with logs and query evidence, isolating product behavior from configuration error.
  • Own implementation decisions. Compare viable techniques within the approved architecture, document measured tradeoffs, and recommend the most maintainable implementation to the responsible architect or technical lead.
  • Accelerate with AI. Use AI tooling - including Data 360 APIs and MCP Servers - to automate the build process and compress customers’ time to value.
  • Co-build and hand off. Work alongside customer technical teams and partners through pairing, code reviews, and configuration reviews. Package reusable metadata, scripts, queries, tests, and runbooks so the solution can be reproduced and supported. Support deployment, validation, production handoff, and early stabilization, leaving clear ownership and known limitations.
  • Feed the roadmap. Surface reproducible platform gaps and edge cases - with live evidence, impact, and expected behavior - directly to Product and Support.



You're Our Person If...

  • You have 8+ years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, or technical implementation, including a production data solution you can explain in detail.
  • You have a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
  • You have hands-on experience implementing Salesforce Data 360 (Data Cloud) or a comparable enterprise data platform across ingestion, modeling, identity, insight, activation, and operations.
  • You have hands-on experience building data pipelines and integrations using at least one enterprise data platform or technology, such as Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, Kafka, cloud object storage, or an enterprise MDM platform.
  • You are proficient in SQL and can build, debug, and optimize multi-table queries, joins, filters, transformations, and validation checks.
  • You are fluent in at least one implementation language used in enterprise delivery - Apex, Java, Python, or JavaScript/TypeScript - and are willing to learn the others as needed.
  • You understand data modeling, APIs, integration patterns, batch and streaming processing, and the practical differences between copied, federated, and Zero Copy data access.
  • You’ve built retrieval systems for AI applications - vector databases, search indexes, embedding pipelines, or knowledge bases - and can explain the design decisions behind chunking, indexing, and relevance.
  • You’ve implemented secure service-to-service integration patterns (OAuth, SAML, event-driven architectures) and are conversant in emerging agent protocols like MCP and agent-to-agent communication.
  • You can implement secure data access and rigorously test it, including permissions, entitlements, consent, user context, restricted populations, and negative test cases.
  • You diagnose technical problems methodically, use logs and query evidence, isolate product behavior from configuration errors, and document a reproducible result.
  • You can implement against a documented architecture, explain what you built to customer technical teams, and recognize when a question requires an architect or security owner.
  • You have delivered alongside customers, partners, professional services, or internal implementation teams in deadline-driven environments.
  • You are excited to work directly with customer administrators, developers, data engineers, and architects.
  • You have relevant certifications in Salesforce Agentforce, Data 360, and the Salesforce Platfororm

title: Software Engineering Architect, PKI & Trust Services
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

Every service on a global, multi-cloud platform rests on one foundation: trust. The systems that issue certificates, establish workload and AI agent identity, and protect cryptographic keys let millions of services prove their identity to one another.


As an Architect, you define the strategy and technical direction for this foundation as the industry moves to shorter certificate lifetimes, fully automated lifecycle management, and post-quantum cryptography.


This is a hands-on architecture role for a distributed-systems leader with strong security depth. You design for continuous global availability, guide the evolution of our cryptography without disrupting dependent services, and implement working systems across multiple engineering teams. Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and key-management expertise are strong advantages, but deep distributed-systems and security judgment matter most.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Own the target architecture and multi-year strategy for certificate lifecycle, trust distribution, and cryptographic identity across workloads and AI agents, and lead execution through production.
  • Architect highly available, globally scalable trust infrastructure with measurable Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and fleet-wide automated certificate renewal capabilities.
  • Drive automation-first, cost-effective architecture focused on zero-touch lifecycle operations, zero-downtime migrations, and data-driven build-versus-buy decisions.
  • Establish architectural and security standards for the interfaces between the trust platform and dependent infrastructure, and guide teams through complex design trade-offs.
  • Stay hands-on by prototyping, writing critical-path code, and validating architecture in live systems.
  • Present investment and architecture proposals to senior leadership, mentor engineering leads, and scale technical expertise across the organization.

You're Our Person If...

  • You have 12+ years of experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems or infrastructure services, with a proven track record of driving multi-team technical strategy into production.
  • You have deep expertise in distributed-systems architecture, reliability, and performance at scale.
  • You have hands-on experience operating mission-critical, highly available services on public cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Kubernetes and service mesh.
  • You have security domain experience in identity and authorization, applied cryptography, or infrastructure security.
  • You have working knowledge of PKI, X.509 certificates, mutual Transport Layer Security (mTLS), and key management.
  • You have proven leadership in aligning cross-organizational initiatives without direct authority.
  • You have strong communication skills, with a track record of authoring adopted architecture proposals and presenting effectively to both engineers and executives.
  • You bring a demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering, using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty.
  • You have experience using AI tools (for example, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor) in development workflows.
  • You hold a related technical degree.

Even Better If...

  • You have built or operated certificate, identity, or key-management services at scale.
  • You are familiar with workload identity standards (for example, Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone (SPIFFE)) and short-lived credentials.
  • You know post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards, such as Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA), and hybrid key exchange in TLS 1.3, as well as emerging approaches like Merkle Tree Certificates and crypto-agility design principles.
  • You have contributed to technical standards bodies (for example, the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), the CA/Browser Forum, or the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)) or to major open-source projects.

To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Sales

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Applications will be accepted until 11/30/2026.

About Salesforce

We’re Salesforce, the Customer Company, inspiring the future of business with AI+ Data +CRM. Leading with our core values, we help companies across every industry blaze new trails and connect with customers in a whole new way. And, we empower you to be a Trailblazer, too — driving your performance and career growth, charting new paths, and improving the state of the world. If you believe in business as the greatest platform for change and in companies doing well and doing good – you’ve come to the right place.

Our Enterprise Business team focuses on working with our most strategic customers and organizations of 10,000+ employees. You will have the opportunity to work in a fast paced team with various customers and receive personalized training and career opportunities.


You will be aligned to the following clouds:

    • Public Sector / State Government / Selling to the Rocky Mountain territory

We're hiring a builder. This Account Executive will own Salesforce's state government business in the Rocky Mountain territory where the white space is real and the relationships are still being written.

These are lean, pragmatic states where agencies do a lot with a little, and where trust is earned in person, over time. There's no inherited book of business to coast on. You'll pick the right agencies, map the people and the money, and turn a handful of first conversations into a durable, multi-agency footprint.


You'll sit on the Public Sector team for the Rocky Mountain region, partnered closely with Solution Engineering, our partner ecosystem and an RVP who is in the field with you. If you want to look back in three years and say "I built that," this is the seat.


What you'll do:

Build the territory plan

• Own a written territory and account plan for the Rocky Mountains that ranks agencies by need, budget timing and executive sponsorship, and update it every quarter.

• Map each priority agency's org chart, budget cycle, legislative calendar and technology debt (legacy case management, mainframe systems, paper-based processes).

• Track biennial budget sessions, federal funding streams and IT modernization initiatives so your pipeline lines up with when money actually moves.

Open doors and earn trust

• Create pipeline from zero through prospecting, events, partner co-selling and relentless follow-through.

• Build relationships with agency heads, CIOs, CFOs, program directors and state IT leadership, and become the person they call when they're thinking about a problem.

• Show up in person. Travel across all three states regularly for executive meetings, site visits, government technology summits and association events.

Run disciplined, complex sales cycles

• Lead long-cycle, multi-stakeholder deals from first discovery through procurement, contracting and launch.

• Navigate public sector buying paths, including cooperative contracts (e.g. NASPO ValuePoint), reseller partners and agency-specific RFPs.

• Shape solutions across Salesforce's platform, including Agentforce, Data Cloud, Service Cloud and industry solutions for Public Sector, with your SE and partners.

• Forecast accurately and keep a clean, honest pipeline in Salesforce.

Land and expand

• Turn first wins into lighthouse references, then use them to expand across agencies and toward enterprise-wide agreements.

• Work with Customer Success and partners to make sure every customer goes live and gets value, because in a small state, every reference travels.

What you bring

• 7+ years of quota-carrying enterprise software sales, with at least 3 selling into state or local government.

• A record of building a territory from scratch. You can walk us through a time you started with no pipeline and a list of names, and what you built from it.

• Exceptional account planning. You think in agency org charts, budget cycles and multi-year roadmaps, and you write plans other people can actually execute against.

• Executive presence. You're credible in the room with a cabinet secretary or state CIO, you listen more than you pitch, and you can tie technology to mission outcomes like faster benefits, shorter wait times and stronger compliance.

• Perseverance. Public sector cycles run 12 to 24 months. You stay curious and consistent through stalled budgets, RFP delays and leadership turnover, and you treat "not yet" as information, not rejection.

• Public sector buying fluency, including RFPs, cooperative purchasing vehicles, reseller partners and the role of the legislature in funding.

• Partner savvy. You know how to co-sell with SIs and resellers and make them want to bring you into their accounts.

• Willingness to travel regularly across WY, ND and SD. Based in or near the territory (or the Rocky Mountain region) is preferred.

Nice to have

• Existing relationships with state agencies in WY, ND, SD or neighboring states.

• Experience selling CRM, case management or platform solutions into Health and Human Services, Labor, Revenue, Transportation or Public Safety.

• Familiarity with modernization themes like legacy mainframe replacement, federal compliance frameworks and AI adoption in government.

• Salesforce ecosystem experience, as a customer, partner or seller.

What success looks like

• First 90 days: a written territory plan, priority agencies identified, and executive meetings on the calendar in all three states.

• First 6 months: qualified pipeline across multiple agencies, with active partner co-sell motions and at least one opportunity in procurement.

• First 12 months: first lighthouse customer signed and live, a reference you can take to the next agency, and a clear path toward a multi-agency agreement.

Why this role

You'll get the autonomy of building something new with the backing of a team that has done it before in neighboring states. You'll have a leader who joins you in the field, an SE partner invested in your wins, and a front-row seat as AI changes how government serves people.


Day to Day

Our Enterprise Account Executives engage with existing customers and new leads to sell the entire Salesforce Customer 360 platform. They build positive, trusted relationships with both key team members and c-suite decision makers within their patch, and become naturals at helping customers realize value from their Salesforce investments.


You will use your skills to develop opportunities, through both warm leads and whitespace prospecting.


      • Develop key customer stakeholder relationships and drive customer satisfaction at assigned accounts
      • Develop and drive the overall long-term strategy for the account, aligned to customer business objectives
      • Coordinate internal Salesforce resources to meet customer business needs
      • Perform account planning at assigned accounts, coordinating with Prime and Cloud sales resources to ensure strategic alignment
      • Share Salesforce value proposition for existing and/or new customers

Working at Salesforce

Working at Salesforce isn’t all about selling. It’s also about learning, and we heavily invest in you with a month-long immersion and onboarding, including: a week-long product bootcamp, mentorship program, weekly coaching and development programs.


Benefits

We are pioneers of the Pledge 1% model, providing product, grants and community service to those in need. We are proud to be#1 in PEOPLE’s Top 50 Companies that Care, and are on Fortune’s Change the World list.

We provide every employee with 7 paid volunteer days off a year, and donation matching for all approved charitable donations.


We provide other world-leading benefits to all our employees, including;

      • Health, life insurance, retirement saving plan
      • Monthly wellness allowance
      • Flexible time off & leave policies
      • Parental benefits
      • Perks and discounts

If you require assistance due to a disability applying for open positions please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.


**This role will be posted until 11/30/2026.

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. DEPARTMENT DESCRIPTION

Salesforce Professional Services - Global Delivery Centre (GDC) focuses on delivering strategic engagements that define transformational opportunities and execution of change programs. We are the trusted delivery partner for Salesforce Professional Services that ensures end to end multi-cloud delivery capabilities across all Salesforce technologies and scales with agility for successful customer outcomes!  We at GDC strive to foster growth & innovation with focus on performance, productivity & impact.


OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE

Our Global Delivery Center is seeking a design-savvy Business Analyst/Solution Consultant to support Solution Delivery opportunities in the Customer Success Group team, lending expertise to the delivery of world-class Salesforce implementations and building the necessary and valuable relationships both internally and externally in order to become recognized as a world class business transformation expert.


YOUR IMPACT

You will be working directly with customers to meet their business needs. You’ll create detailed requirement documentation and coordinate development of comprehensive assets to run on the OmniStudio Platform. Through the work on Salesforce Industries, you’ll become a guide in educating the customer about product capabilities, identifying gaps in the processes, and servicing customers via digital channels. You shall also develop leadership skills in Agile software development.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Working closely with our customers, industry experts, product managers, and engineers to investigate business processes at a detailed level.
  • Participating in business process redesign, roadmap planning, and identifying touch points in multi-cloud implementations.
  • Developing strong client relationships by building trust, rapport and positive working relationships with both internal and external customers, and team members.
  • Create prototypes, proof of concepts and sample mockups as a means of eliciting and defining business requirements.
  • Crafting and owning user stories/business requirements documents as an outcome of the requirements gathering sessions, and detailing out the user stories in the agile sprints for the scrum team to work upon.
  • Collaborating with SFI’s product and design teams to suggest improvements, find opportunities for automation, understand the standard methodologies and create simple and sophisticated flows that deliver the functionality required.
  • Utilising knowledge on OmniStudio tools, including OmniScript, FlexCards, Integration Procedures to rapidly construct dynamic, omni-channel interactions.
  • Attending daily stand-ups, story pointing meetings, sprint planning, and retrospectives to ensure progress on requests and removal of blockers.
  • As required, participating in the UAT and release process, including test planning, development of test scripts, testing logistics, test execution, and status reporting.
  • Analyzing the data requirements, structures and integration points of the process, and creating mapping to Salesforce Industry objects or external REST endpoints.
  • Documenting work using flow charts, written descriptions, screenshots and videos.
  • Reacting to process and product related questions and raising issues to the correct team or to the management as required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • +3 years of experience in enterprise software as business/functional analyst or product owner.
  • Salesforce Platform experience.
  • Demonstrated capability to understand business strategies and application objectives, and translate those requirements into effective process designs.
  • Excellent design skills, including the ability to critique visual elements and optimize user flows.
  • Excellent written and graphic communication skills, clearly document requirements and process assets using text, diagrams and videos.
  • English advanced skills.
  • Expertise in process modeling tools and standard methodologies.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge of Salesforce Industries.
  • Insurance, Health or Telecommunications industry experience is appreciated.
  • Hands-on experience of CPQ, EPC
  • Knowledge of design thinking processes and tools.
  • Experience working with Scrum teams and Agile Methodology.
  • Certified Product Owner.

title: Staff Data Engineer - Slack
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience


The Metrics Foundations team sits within Slack's Data Engineering organization in Data & Insights, building the trusted datasets and metrics that power decisions across Product, Analytics, Marketing, Sales, and Operations. The team partners with Product, Data Science, Analytics, and Engineering to define and govern metrics with consistent quality and clear service level agreements (SLAs).


Increasingly, AI agents and developer tools consume these metrics alongside people, so you build the trusted, machine-readable foundation that maps business questions to the right metric definitions and tables. As a Staff Data Engineer, you set the technical direction for how Slack defines, computes, governs, and serves its most critical metrics, and you serve as the technical lead for Agentic Analytics on the metrics side.


This is a senior individual contributor role with organization-wide scope and multi-quarter impact.


What You'll Actually Be Doing


  • Set the architecture and roadmap for the metrics platform, from ingestion and canonical datasets to the semantic layer and serving, making clear tradeoffs between freshness, accuracy, reliability, and cost.
  • Design and scale data models and pipelines that turn billions of records into trusted datasets with measurable quality, predictable SLAs, and freshness signals for consumers.
  • Evolve the semantic layer and build the APIs and tools that let people and AI agents navigate metric definitions, lineage, and ownership, and draft accurate queries.
  • Lead metric certification, governance, and design reviews, and mentor senior engineers, using AI-assisted development to deliver faster without compromising quality.


You're Our Person If...


  • You have 10+ years of software or data engineering experience, including 6+ years hands-on with data architecture, data modeling, and metadata management.
  • You have led complex, multi-team technical initiatives as an individual contributor and drive alignment across Engineering, Product, Data Science, and Analytics without formal authority.
  • You have deep SQL expertise, strong Python skills, and working proficiency in Go, Java, or Scala, with a record of architecting scalable, cost-efficient data models and pipelines.
  • You have hands-on experience with Spark, Trino, Airflow, Iceberg, and Snowflake, and with dimensional and star/snowflake modeling.
  • A related technical degree required.


Even Better If...


  • You have experience building infrastructure or tools for AI agents, such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, tool-use APIs, or evaluation harnesses.
  • You have experience with semantic layers, metrics platforms, data catalogs, or lineage tools such as dbt, sqlmesh, Datahub, Cube, or LookML.
  • You have experience with experimentation platforms, including metrics, exposure logging, and guardrails for A/B testing.

descriptionHtml:

Job Details

About Salesforce

The Experience

The Authentication Platform team owns the core identity services for Salesforce's production infrastructure — the Production IAM stack. The portfolio spans Kerberos-based authentication, TOTP, and FIDO2/WebAuthn, bridging legacy infrastructure protocols and modern cloud-native identity standards. Because the platform is a tier-0 dependency for the entire company, we run at massive throughput with a 4+ nines availability target across Public Cloud (AWS/GCP) and hybrid deployments on Kubernetes, with modern CI/CD. Our security posture is Zero Trust and least-privilege by default, and we partner closely with security architects on identity verification and credential-handling design.

You'll work on services in the Production IAM stack as an individual contributor — implementing features across the Kerberos, TOTP, and FIDO2/WebAuthn service portfolio, contributing to designs that senior engineers lead, and taking on-call for a tier-0 platform. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on strong execution, growing technical depth in identity protocols, and shipping high-quality, well-tested code in a security-critical environment.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Deliver features across the Authentication Platform's service portfolio - Kerberos, TOTP, FIDO2/WebAuthn - writing clean, well-tested backend code in Java, Go, or C#.
  • Contribute to design specs and research spikes for features in your area, alongside more senior engineers who lead the design.
  • Implement identity and federation protocols used by the platform, including Kerberos, LDAP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, and TOTP. Familiarity with SAML/OIDC is useful for interop conversations with adjacent teams.
  • Partner with the Product Owner and tech lead on story-level scope, sequencing, and dependencies for your own work, and help refine and clarify work items before they land in a sprint.
  • Reliably deliver as a developer, reviewer, and tester — high test coverage, clean code, and reviews that catch issues before they land, with a security-first mindset appropriate for tier-0 services.
  • Apply Salesforce engineering best practices to code, tests, and CI/CD pipelines. Leave code in better shape than you found it.
  • Use AI development tools (e.g.Claude Code) in your day-to-day workflow, and critically evaluate both human and AI-generated code for correctness, performance, and security compliance.
  • Analyze and fix bugs in your area, working with more senior engineers on the complex ones. Debug production issues and drive them to a fix.
  • Exhibit ownership beyond just coding your features — an active role in testing, review, and monitoring is part of the job, especially given the tier-0 nature of the platform.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for the Authentication Platform and handle common alerts confidently. On-call is a real, high-visibility part of this role because of the platform's tier-0 status.
  • Understand the platform's telemetry — metrics, logs, traces, SLIs — and extend it for the features you own. The availability target is 4+ nines.
  • Contribute to Root Cause Analyses for incidents in your area, and follow through on assigned action items.
  • Work with internal stakeholders — service teams and infrastructure owners who depend on the Authentication Platform — to answer integration questions about the features you own.
  • Author and maintain technical documentation and runbooks for your work.



You're Our Person If...

  • Strong programming ability in Java, Go, or C#, with production experience building backend services.
  • Working knowledge of at least one identity or federation protocol from this set: Kerberos, LDAP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, TOTP, SAML, OIDC. Deeper experience in one or more is a plus.
  • Experience building, deploying, and debugging distributed services in a Public Cloud environment (AWS or GCP) or a hybrid deployment, using Kubernetes and modern CI/CD.
  • Solid grasp of software fundamentals: data structures, testing, code review, source control, CI/CD, and Agile execution as a team member.
  • A security-first mindset — writing code with least-privilege defaults, threat-aware reviews, and thorough automated testing appropriate for identity-critical systems.
  • Ability to debug production issues in a distributed system using logs, metrics, and traces.
  • Comfortable executing an agreed-upon plan largely independently, escalating design-level and cross-cutting decisions to senior engineers.



Even Better If...

  • IAM specialist depth — familiarity with the internals of one or more of Kerberos, LDAP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, TOTP, and the interop story with SAML/OIDC.
  • Security hardening — familiarity with HSMs, PKI, and secure credential storage patterns.
  • Compliance and auditing — exposure to controls and evidence requirements under PCI, SOC 2, or HIPAA.
  • Operational grit — experience on-call for a high-visibility production service, and comfort debugging live incidents under pressure.
  • Experience integrating AI development tools into engineering workflows, including prompt design and reviewing AI-generated code for security-critical systems.



Education

  • Master's degree (or foreign equivalent) in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, or a related field. A Bachelor's degree (or foreign equivalent) is acceptable with additional years of experience.



Minimum years of experience

  • 5 years of software engineering experience

  • Build (Product Engineering): Design, build, and ship AI-powered products, developing technical expertise in production-scale engineering.
  • Shape (Product Management): Translate customer needs into product strategy, define priorities, and help shape the next generation of AI products.
  • Deliver (FDE / Builders): Work with teams developing and deploying AI solutions that solve real-world customer challenges.
  • Transform (DET / Customer Zero): Reimagine enterprise workflows and operations, leveraging AI to drive transformation at scale.

While you'll spend the summer gaining hands-on experience in one discipline, you'll also collaborate with interns across the other three disciplines on a cross-functional capstone project. Together, you'll bring engineering, product strategy, customer solutions, and enterprise transformation perspectives to a shared AI challenge, culminating in a final presentation at Demo Day.


The internship provides an opportunity to build technical depth, develop a broader understanding of the AI lifecycle, and experience how cross-functional teams bring innovative solutions to life.

Strong foundation in data structures, algorithms, software engineering, and technical problem-solving.
  • Practical Coding Experience: Experience developing software through academic projects, research, internships, or independent technical projects.

  • Product influence: Experience synthesizing customer needs across markets into prioritized product recommendations and collaborating with product management to influence roadmaps.

The Experience

We are seeking a lead full stack engineer with enterprise software engineering experience to drive the architecture, technical roadmap, and execution for our next-generation Security Assurance Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform. In this role, you will hold end-to-end technical ownership over the platform’s core engines—including policy as code, compliance as code, automated evidence collection, telemetry and alerting, and risk evaluation modules.

Beyond hands-on development in Python, Java, and modern front-end frameworks, you will act as a primary technical leader: defining system architecture, scoping and planning multi-quarter technical initiatives, and guiding distributed feature teams from concept through deployment. You will also pioneer the team’s operational strategy around AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude, Gemini, OpenAI) to accelerate output and elevate code quality across the engineering organization.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • End-to-End Ownership: Take technical ownership of complex, multi-system initiatives, driving architectural decisions, technical specifications, phase planning, and execution across the delivery lifecycle.
  • Architecture & System Design: Architect resilient, cloud-native microservice architectures that process large-scale compliance telemetry, support automated evidence ingestion, and execute low-latency risk evaluation engines.

About the team

We are looking for a technically strong Security Governance professional who can bridge the gap between Security & Compliance requirements and Engineering implementation.


This role will serve as the technical voice and face of Assurance. You will partner closely with Engineering organizations, PCLs, Product Security, Legal, and other stakeholders to understand how security and compliance requirements are implemented in real systems. You will identify what is working and what is not, and translate those insights back into practical, scalable governance requirements.


The successful candidate will understand systems and architectures well enough to move beyond validating whether a control exists. They will evaluate how the control is designed, implemented, operated, and scaled across the enterprise.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Support Assurance and Engineering Alignment - Support technical liaison activities between Assurance, Engineering, Product Security, PCLs, and Legal, ensuring governance requirements are clearly understood and actionable.
  • Evaluate Control Implementation - Work directly with Engineering teams to understand how security and compliance controls are implemented within applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud environments, and engineering workflows.
  • Create the Engineering Feedback Loop - Assess what is working, what is creating unnecessary friction, and where controls or requirements are unclear or difficult to operationalize. Feed those insights back into control design, standards, and governance processes.
  • Make Requirements Engineer-Usable - Translate regulatory, compliance, and security expectations into clear, actionable technical requirements that Engineering teams can consistently implement and validate.
  • Develop Second-Line Oversight - Execute second-line oversight protocols that independently monitor, audit, and validate that all security controls are operational across engineering teams in Salesforce (e.g., attestations, CRE checks).
  • Understand Systems End-to-End - Develop a deep understanding of key platforms, architectures, engineering processes, security capabilities, and control implementations to help Assurance make better risk and compliance decisions.
  • Assess Risk in M&A - Assess control and risk exposure during M&As. Design the assessment to price risk, evaluate compatibility, and deliver an executable activation plan tied back to the risk model.
  • Partner on Emerging Security Requirements - Collaborate with Product Security, Legal, PCEs, Market Enablement, and other teams to understand emerging requirements and determine how they should translate into future security controls and engineering expectations.
  • Track the Direction of Compliance Frameworks - Monitor where regulatory and compliance expectations are heading, including AI governance, the EU AI Act, evolving international requirements, and market-specific regulatory expectations. Proactively identify implications for the organization.
  • Support Enablement and Change Management - Contribute to change management efforts, documentation, and training to help engineering teams understand and comply with relevant policies and standards.
  • Support Control Incident Response - Participate in control incident reviews and postmortems, assisting with root-cause analysis and tracking remediation efforts for control failures.
  • Contribute to Control Refinement - Collaborate with control owners to provide feedback on control effectiveness and suggest updates based on operational findings and engineering feedback.
  • Engage Security Champions - Work alongside security and control champions across Engineering to gather feedback, distribute guidance, and support governance adoption.
  • Support Leadership Reporting - Help track and report metrics on control coverage, compliance trends, and risk items to support management reporting.
  • Represent Assurance Requirements - Serve as a point of contact for Assurance in engineering and operational discussions, helping integrate compliance considerations early in development cycles.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required. We're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • Relevant experience or technical background in security engineering, cloud security, product security, IAM, platform engineering, or IT governance.
  • Ability to understand complex systems, architectures, APIs, infrastructure, cloud environments, and software development processes.
  • Experience translating security, risk, regulatory, or compliance requirements into technical implementation requirements.
  • Strong understanding of security controls and frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC, SOX, FedRAMP, or similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with emerging technology and regulatory areas such as AI security, AI governance, privacy, and evolving global technology regulations.
  • Ability to work effectively with Engineering while also partnering with Legal, Compliance, Security, Risk, and business stakeholders.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical implementation details to governance teams and translate governance expectations into language Engineering teams can act on.
  • Analytical mindset with the ability to evaluate requirements and provide constructive input based on practical constraints.
  • Experience with independent control testing, assurance or audit practices, incident or root-cause analysis, or M&A due diligence is a plus.

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means creating a strong connection between what Assurance requires and what Engineering can effectively implement. Controls become more technically relevant, and requirements become easier for Engineering teams to consume. Implementation challenges are identified earlier, and emerging security and regulatory expectations are incorporated into the control environment before they become compliance gaps. Control failures are handled with the same rigor as availability incidents, and leadership has clear visibility into control reliability and systemic risk.


Ultimately, this role will help move Assurance from primarily validating compliance to becoming a technical governance partner that actively shapes secure and compliant engineering practices by design.

descriptionHtml:

About Salesforce

About the team


Assurance at Salesforce is being rebuilt as an engineering discipline. Legacy GRC runs on spreadsheets, screenshots, and an annual scramble to prove controls worked months ago. We're replacing it with a model that is continuous, automated, and built into how Salesforce ships. Controls are code. Evidence comes from pipelines, not people chasing tickets.

  • Risk-informed, control managed. We monitor, validate, and improve the controls that stand against threats and failures.
  • Visibility and invention. We give Salesforce a clear, current view of its security posture, and we invest in the people who build it.
  • Always in front. Nothing waits for the next audit to surface.

You'll have real ownership, a real roadmap, and the chance to define what modern assurance looks like for the industry.


What you'll be doing:


As a Sr. Security Governance Engineer, you'll translate enterprise security policies, regulatory requirements, and risk expectations into measurable, technically actionable controls. You'll help build a governance framework where policies and standards are version-controlled, validated, and integrated into engineering workflows. Over time, you'll grow into a Security Control Family Owner for domains such as IAM, Cloud, Application Security, Cryptography, Data Protection, or Infrastructure Security. The focus is governance, control design, and policy ownership. It is not hands-on software development.

  • Policy and standards: Develop and maintain security policies, technical standards, and control requirements. Manage the policy lifecycle: versioning, approvals, exceptions, reviews, and change management. Keep them aligned with architecture, risk appetite, and regulatory obligations.
  • Governance-as-Code / Policy-as-Code: Define structured, machine-readable policy and control requirements. Work with engineering to turn them into guardrails and validation criteria, using tools like OPA/Rego or cloud-native policy frameworks. You won't necessarily own the implementation. Review implementations for alignment with policy intent.
  • Control framework: Maintain a common control framework with clear objectives, ownership, and validation criteria. Establish traceability from regulation to policy to control to implementation. Set expectations for preventive, detective, and compensating controls, and support continuous evaluation of control effectiveness.
  • Control family ownership: Act as the SME and point of contact for your assigned domains. Interpret regulations, assess gaps, exceptions, and emerging risks, and recommend improvements.
  • Collaboration: Work with Security Engineering, Product Security, Cloud Security, IAM, Compliance, Risk, Audit, Legal, and business teams. Bring a governance perspective to architecture and design discussions.

Expected Outcomes

  • Decision speed: Rules are obvious, decisions are fast, and outputs are predictable, with governance built into the engineering workflow.
  • Scalable governance: Policies and control requirements are clear, consistent, and technically actionable.
  • Governance-as-Code adoption: Requirements are version-controlled, traceable, and integrated into security practices.
  • Alignment and visibility: Written policies, technical guardrails, and implemented controls match. Regulations, risks, controls, and evidence are clearly linked.
  • Control family SMEs: Dedicated owners set policy direction and technical standards for each domain.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required — we're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 2+ years in information security governance, security engineering, technology risk, or related functions
  • Strong grasp of security policies, standards, control frameworks, and governance processes
  • Familiarity with NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or PCI DSS
  • Ability to turn regulatory and security requirements into measurable control objectives
  • Working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP), IAM, application, infrastructure, and data security
  • Understanding of control design (preventive and detective), risk assessment, and exception management
  • Familiarity with modern development practices, cloud environments, and CI/CD
  • Strong analytical, communication, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Governance-as-Code or Policy-as-Code, and policy engines such as OPA/Rego or HashiCorp Sentinel
  • Familiarity with YAML, JSON, Git, infrastructure-as-code, and DevSecOps
  • Experience with GRC platforms, Common Controls Frameworks (CCF), and OSCAL
  • Exposure to security posture management, compliance validation, architecture reviews, or AI governance

How We Work:

  • Engineering-first. We use version control, code review, CI/CD, and backlogs. Assurance work ships like software.
  • Automate first. If it's done manually twice, it's a candidate for a build.
  • Signals, not surprises. Gaps become alerts and workflows, and control failures resolve through defined escalation paths.
  • Embedded partners. We work alongside T&P teams as peers, not gatekeepers, and solve problems with them, not at them.
  • Outcomes over activity. We measure risk reduced, effort saved, and audit friction removed.
  • Room to grow. Learn the engineering side if you come from GRC, or the risk side if you come from engineering. We support both paths.

Contentful is looking for a Software Engineer to join our Applied AI product line with a primary focus on Marketplace. In this role, you will help build, maintain, and grow the systems, apps, and workflows that expand what customers can do with Contentful.

  • Solid professional software engineering experience building and maintaining production systems.
  • Strong experience with TypeScript and Node.js, plus solid experience building user-facing product surfaces in React or similar front-end frameworks.

  • Experience designing and evolving APIs, integrations, and services used by other engineers, partners, or customers.
  • Good judgment around reliability, maintainability, security, and technical tradeoffs in a product environment.
  • Comfort working across the stack and across boundaries, from user experience to backend behavior to operational concerns.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, including experience working cross-functionally and asynchronously across teams and time zones.
  • A product mindset and real empathy for developers, partners, and customers.
  • Practical experience using AI tools to improve engineering productivity, with the ability to evaluate outputs critically and maintain a high quality bar.

  • Experience with developer platforms, SDKs, app frameworks, marketplaces, extensibility products, or integration ecosystems.
  • Experience with AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Cloudflare, or related cloud infrastructure.
  • Experience maintaining or contributing to public or shared developer tooling.

Production experience required. Builder mindset non-negotiable.

The FDE Voice is a hands-on Forward Deployed Engineer role with a special focus on Voice. In this role, you will work directly with customers to design, build, and deploy AI-powered voice experiences in production, using Agentforce Voice, Service Cloud Voice, and contact center telephony integrations. You will own the full delivery cycle, from discovery and solution design to configuration, testing, and go-live, and you will be responsible for voice-specific quality, including latency, call flow logic, interruption handling, multilingual performance, and seamless escalation to human agents. You will act as a direct bridge between customers and the Voice Product team: sharing structured feedback from live deployments, raising product gaps and feature requests, contributing to roadmap discussions, and participating in early access programs and pilots to validate new capabilities in real customer environments. Working closely with customer teams, Product, and the wider EMEA South FDE team, you will turn field learnings into reusable voice patterns and assets that accelerate future deployments.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Develop AI agents and experiences that take real actions for real organisations. Our solutions are in production at some of the largest enterprises on the planet. The work matters because the customers depend on it.
  • Design agent intelligence: prompts, reasoning, tool calls, and integration with customer systems, leveraging our Agentic AI platform and current LLM techniques.
  • Own technical components end-to-end: from architecture choice to deployed, validated, and observable in production.
  • Build and integrate data pipelines on Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer data platforms. Model the data, ship the pipeline, and validate the output.
  • Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes.
  • Contribute to proofs-of-concept and MVPs that move from sketch to deployable in days, not months.
  • Co-build alongside customers and partners, sharing best practices and enablement as you go. Leaving teams more capable after each engagement than before.
  • Surface platform gaps, edge cases, and field insights to senior Engineers and the product team. Your real-world experience is the product feedback loop.
  • Partner with the Deployment Strategist in your pod to translate customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.

  • You have prior customer-facing technical delivery experience (consulting, professional services, or forward deployed engineering) — this is a requirement, not a nice-to-have.
  • You're fluent in at least one of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Apex — and willing to add to that list as the work demands.
  • You've been hands-on with LLMs and prompt engineering. You can explain why a prompt failed and what you'd change.
  • You understand data modelling, APIs, and integration patterns deeply enough to design them, not just consume them.
  • You can hold your own in a room with sales teams and customer architects.
  • You ship quality code and evaluate AI outputs with engineering rigour.

  • You thrive in the group chat that's building something, not just talking about it.
  • You're excited to travel ~25% of the time and work directly alongside customers.

The Experience

The software engineer role at Salesforce encompasses architecture, design, implementation, and testing to ensure we build products right and release them with high quality. Equally important is advanced prompt engineering — the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready.

We pride ourselves on writing high-quality, maintainable code that strengthens the stability of the product and makes our work easier. We embrace the hybrid model and celebrate the individual strengths of each team member while helping everyone on the team grow into the best version of themselves. We believe that autonomous teams with the freedom to make decisions empower individuals, the product, the company, and the customers we serve to thrive.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Design, build, test, and operate capabilities across the Momentum product, from meeting capture and recording through transcript processing, insight generation, and customer-facing experiences.
  • Develop robust backend services, APIs, and event-driven workflows that perform reliably at enterprise scale in a multi-tenant environment.
  • Contribute to frontend experiences using modern JavaScript and component-based frameworks, including Lightning Web Components where applicable.
  • Process and manage high-volume conversation, recording, transcript, and insight data securely and efficiently.
  • Design for security, privacy, compliance, data residency, observability, and operational readiness from the beginning.
  • Apply test-driven development practices and contribute to unit, integration, functional, performance, and end-to-end test coverage.
  • Use CI/CD tooling and modern engineering practices to safely deliver production-grade software.
  • Monitor production behavior, diagnose complex distributed-system failures, and improve system reliability and supportability.
  • Participate in architecture and code reviews, critically evaluating human- and AI-generated code for correctness, maintainability, security, accessibility, and performance.
  • Use AI development tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor to improve development velocity, testing, debugging, and documentation.
  • Create clear system context, including architecture decisions, operational constraints, coding standards, and runbooks, so both engineers and AI-assisted workflows can operate effectively.
  • Collaborate with Product, Design, Security, Privacy, Site Reliability, and partner engineering teams to deliver trusted customer outcomes.



You're Our Person If...

  • A related technical degree, or equivalent practical experience, required
  • 8+ years of backend software development experience
  • Deep knowledge of object-oriented programming languages: Java, C++, Go, C#, Ruby, Scala, Python, Node.js, or JavaScript
  • Broad knowledge of web standards relating to APIs such as REST, SOAP, XML, WSDL, HTTP, JSON, etc.
  • Experience with Spring, gRPC, REST, and the HTTP protocol
  • Experience with Agile development methodology
  • A demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering — using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, etc.) in development workflows
  • Advanced prompt engineering skills and the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready
  • Willingness to participate in the team's on-call rotation to address complex problems in real time and keep services operational and highly available
  • Office-Flex: 10 days per quarter



Even Better If...

  • Experience with conversation intelligence, audio or video recording, transcription, media processing, or meeting-platform integrations
